title: Tate line tensor membership in the fixed integral closed model
statement: For a prime l, finite extension E of Q_l, scheme X with l invertible in every residue field, integer m and an intrinsically integral constructible derived object M [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], tensor M with the degree-zero integralTwistLine l E X m using the integralClosed.tensor of the fixed coefficientDerivedSystemEvaluationCalculus. The resulting object is intrinsically integral constructible. This only concerns membership; it includes no pullback, cofinal transport, tower isomorphism or realization claim. Coefficient fields, completed coefficient sheaves, strict systems and the fixed derived presentations are as in [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], [def-sp-twisted-pullback-reduction-data], [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], [def-coef-derived-system-calculus-data].

proof.text: The completed first Tate line is locally free of rank one and has finite locally constant reductions. Apply the integral signed-line reduction/restriction theorem; its PreservesIntegral clause gives integral constructibility of ordinary derived tensor with every signed power.

proof.text: On a K-flat representative of M and the flat degree-zero signed line, the ordinary derived tensor and the fixed integralClosed tensor are localizations of the same total sheaf tensor. The universal derived tensor comparison and single localization identify them. The signed-power definition identifies the line with integralTwistLine for negative, zero and positive integers. Transport the constructibility predicate through this isomorphism.
